title: architecture-review-kv-cache-multi-tenant-routing-notes-2026-04-28
content:
Architecture review notes: KV cache multi-tenant routing (RFC review)

Date: 2026-04-28
Attendees: Priya Shah (owner), Miguel Torres, Lina Becker, Samir Patel, Jordan Lee, Claire Nguyen, + SRE on rotation (TBD)
Moderator: Priya

Agenda:
- Quick recap of current KV cache prototype and motivation for multi-tenant routing
- Review proposed routing policy alternatives from RFC-142
- Discuss isolation/sharding strategies and eviction interactions
- Operational concerns: metrics, rollout/canary, failure modes and fallback policies
- Decide on next steps and owners

Recap / Context:
- Goal: support multi-tenant workloads on shared KV cache with predictable latency and isolation guarantees while maximizing hit-rate and cost efficiency.
- Current prototype (branch: kv-cache-multi-tenant) implements a namespace-per-tenant plus dynamic routing that can route requests to dedicated cache shards or shared shards depending on tenant SLA and recent traffic. Prototype issues: cross-tenant spillover during high load, cold-start penalties when routing between shared <-> dedicated, and uneven hot-key distribution across shards.
- RFC-142 proposed three routing alternatives (A/B/C) and a fallback policy:
  - A: Tenant-first namespace sharding (per-tenant hash -> dedicated/dynamically allocated shards). Strong isolation, higher memory footprint.
  - B: Hybrid hotspot routing (global shared shards + pinning for hot keys). Better memory usage, complexity in pin/unpin.
  - C: Logical namespaces with eviction lanes (shared physical shards, per-tenant eviction quotas). Good fairness but risk of higher miss-rate for bursty tenants.

Decision summary (consensus):
- We tentatively agreed to move forward with a hybrid approach (combination of A and B) as the default routing policy for initial rollout: global shared shards for baseline traffic with a pinning mechanism to allocate dedicated slots for observed hot keys and optionally dedicated shards for enterprise tenants with reserved capacity.
- Rationale: Hybrid balances operational cost and isolation. Full per-tenant dedicated shards (A) is too expensive for most tenants; pure shared-with-eviction (C) risks QoS regressions for enterprise customers.

Detailed decisions and design notes:
1) Namespace model:
- Use logical namespaces per tenant (kv:tenant_id:prefix) to keep key-space clear and support simple metrics per-tenant. This remains consistent with existing prototype.
- Physical placement: default mapping routes to shared shard pool. Tenants with reserved capacity or explicit SLA will be assigned dedicated shard pools.

2) Hot-key detection + pinning:
- Implement continuous hot-key detection in router (moving-window counter + sketch for memory efficiency). Thresholds: default 99th-percentile tokens > X req/s (TBD) -> candidate for pinning.
- Pinning semantics: pin specific keys into a small dedicated pin cache in shared shards (lock with TTL). Pin TTL will be adaptive: initial TTL = 15m, extend on repeated accesses.
- Pin eviction policy: LRU within pinned slots; pinned slots counted separately from per-tenant eviction quota.

3) Dedicated shard reservation:
- Enterprise tenants (on Dedicated plan) can request dedicated shards. Auto-reservation policy for tenants that sustain > Y RPS over M minutes (operational thresholds to be determined in follow-up).
- We will expose a CLI/admin API to force-move a tenant to dedicated shards for troubleshooting.

4) Eviction model and fairness:
- Shared-shard eviction uses a two-tier eviction: (1) per-tenant soft quota enforced via token-bucket-like counters, (2) global LRU across tenants when global pressure high.
- Soft quota default derived from tenant recent usage percentage of cluster capacity. Buckets recomputed every 5m.
- Rationale: prevents a bursty tenant from evicting another tenant's working set entirely.

5) Fallbacks and graceful degradation:
- On cache overload (latency > SLO or memory pressure > threshold): router will progressively shift traffic to model serving without cache (bypass) for the worst offenders, and selectively disable pinning.
- Maintain a prioritized fallback list (dedicated -> shared pinned -> shared -> bypass).

Operational and rollout plan:
- Metrics to instrument before canary:
  - per-tenant cache hit-rate (5m/1h), per-tenant tail-latency (p50/p95/p99), memory usage per shard, number of pinned keys, pin eviction rate, cross-tenant eviction events.
  - SLOs: p99 < 15ms on cache hit for shared shards (target), p99 < 10ms for dedicated shards.
- Canary plan:
  - Stage 1 (internal): enable hybrid routing for non-critical internal tenants (dev/test) for 48h, monitor metrics.
  - Stage 2 (beta): enable for small subset (~5%) of production tenants with opt-in toggles.
  - Stage 3: expand to all hosted tenants, but do not automatically migrate to dedicated shards until manual approval.
- Rollback strategy: immediate revert to current prototype routing + flush pinned slots. Additionally, we will support selective tenant rollback to shared-only routing.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Thresholds for hot-key detection and pin TTL defaults (action: Samir to propose calibration tests).
- Precise billing/chargeback model for pin usage and dedicated shard consumption (action: Claire + Product to define).
- Memory accounting for pinned slots vs tenant quota: should pinned slots be charged to tenant or to global pool? (tentative: charge to tenant if pinned via dedicated reservation, otherwise global pool)
- Impact on KV-cache persistence and prefetching: do we pre-populate pins when migrating shards? Need cross-team sync with serving-runtime prefetcher.

Action items (owner — due):
- Samir Patel — run simulation workload to calibrate hot-key thresholds and provide recommended defaults (due: 2026-05-07).
- Miguel Torres — add per-tenant metrics (hit-rate + tail-latency) to telemetry dashboard and create alerts for cross-tenant eviction events (due: 2026-05-05).
- Lina Becker — prototype pinning TTL adaptive algorithm and push small PoC in branch kv-pinning (due: 2026-05-12).
- Jordan Lee — write initial canary runbook and rollback steps; coordinate with SRE for on-call coverage during Stage 1 (due: 2026-05-04).
- Claire Nguyen + Product — define billing semantics for pinned slots and dedicated shard reservations and share recommendation (due: 2026-05-14).
- Priya Shah — update RFC-142 with hybrid design decisions and link to this meeting notes (due: 2026-05-03).

Notes to self / TODO in doc:
- Add sequence diagram for routing decision path (shared -> pin -> dedicated -> bypass).
- Add cost model appendix: cost per shard, expected memory overhead for pinning at different thresholds.
- Follow up meeting: schedule 2 weeks after PoC metrics are in (suggest 2026-05-20).

References and links:
- RFC-142 (kv-cache sharding + routing): https://confluence.redwood.internal/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=kv-cache-rfc-142
- Prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/tree/kv-cache-multi-tenant
- Related discussion: Linear INF-586 (tenant isolation), GitHub PR #987

Meeting closed at 11:40am PT. Next sync: tentative 2026-05-20 (post calibration results).

Raw/brainstorm fragments (informal):
- "We should avoid per-tenant shard explosion — needs cap" — Miguel
- "Pinning TTL so far feels magic; short TTLs + reinforcement is probably safer than long TTLs" — Lina
- "Billing: customers will expect transparency; track pinned-slot-days" — Claire
- "If a tenant is bursty but low baseline, pinning could thrash; prefer pin only after sustained hotness" — Samir
- Unresolved UX: do we expose pin hints in SDK or keep internal? (prefer internal for now)

Status: notes saved as draft; will update RFC-142 and push design diagrams after PoC results.
